claims.claim: Origen of Alexandria was an early Christian theologian and biblical scholar, born c. 185 and died c. 254.
The Homilies on Joshua were among the last homilies Origen gave before his torture and death during the Decian persecution, around 254.

Origen delivered the homilies to exhort his hearers to persevere in their struggles to overcome the enemies of their souls, using the story of Israel entering the promised land as an allegory for the Christian life from baptism to resurrection.
Origen's hearers included priests whom he urged to illuminate the path for others.
Others wrote down Origen's words as he exhorted, words he had asked the people to pray for and the Spirit to supply.
Most of the original Greek writings were lost during the centuries when Origen was officially defamed.
What survives today is the Latin translation by Rufinus, which forms the basis of modern English translations.
Barbara J. Bruce discusses and affirms the reliability of Rufinus's Latin text in her introduction to the English translation.
